summary.headline: Usha Martin Q4 FY26 operating EBITDA rose 52% to INR 212 crore at a 21.6% margin on revenue up 9.3% to INR 979 crore.
summary.overview: Q4 FY26 consolidated revenue rose 9.3% YoY to INR 979 crore, with operating EBITDA up 52% to INR 212 crore and margin at 21.6%, the highest since the steel business sale. FY26 revenue reached INR 3,691 crore (+6.2%) with operating EBITDA of INR 705 crore (19.1% margin vs 17.2%). Rope volume growth was only about 5% in Q4 because Middle East demand fell short by roughly 900 tons, and LRPC revenue fell 20.4%. The company ended FY26 with a net cash position of INR 332 crore, standalone operations debt-free, and guided to 10-12% volume growth and a 20% margin benchmark.

financial_highlights.metric: Operating cash flow / free cash flow (FY26)
financial_highlights.value: INR 736 crore / INR 457 crore after capex of INR 198 crore

financial_highlights.change: vs net debt of INR 63 crore last year

segments.name: Wire Rope
segments.commentary: Q4 revenue up about 14.8% YoY; FY26 revenue up about 8%. Rope volume grew about 5% in Q4, versus about 8% had Middle East shortfall of roughly 900 tons not occurred. International wire rope prices exceeded INR 300,000 per ton for the first time.

segments.name: Wire
segments.commentary: Q4 revenue up 31.2% YoY; FY26 revenue up about 24%. Input cost increases were passed through with margins not affected.

segments.name: LRPC
segments.commentary: Q4 revenue down 20.4% YoY. Management expects about 48,000 tons of black LRPC in FY27, similar to last year, and 5,000-6,000 tons of plasticated LRPC against 6,000 tons per annum capacity.

segments.name: International business
segments.commentary: Now 57% of total topline versus 55% last year. Europe about 26% of topline; US rose to 9% of topline from 7%.

guidance_outlook: Volume growth target of 10-12% across rope, specialized wires and plasticated LRPC for the next 2-3 years, per management.
Operating margin benchmark raised to a minimum of 20%, from the earlier 18-19% range; management said margins will vary with product mix quarter to quarter.

Capex of about INR 300 crore over the next 2 years for elevator rope capacity (about 6,000 tons of rope capacity, 70-75% of the spend), specialized wires and plasticated LRPC; funded from internal accruals.
Plasticated LRPC volume expected to rise from about 2,500 tons a year to 4,000-4,500 tons once pending customer approvals convert to orders, with capacity to be stepped up to 8,000-9,000 tons later.
Thailand plant modernization expected to show significant operating improvement over about 18 months.
Evaluating selective organic and inorganic opportunities where footprint is limited, particularly in value-added rigging.
risks_watch: Middle East conflict: slower customer activity, project delays and shipment disruption in Dubai and Saudi Arabia; Q4 rope volume shortfall of about 900 tons.
Input cost pressure: steel, gas, LPG (INR 120,000-130,000 per ton) and logistics costs rising since January; pass-through timing could squeeze margins.
Volume vs mix trade-off: management is targeting both 10-12% volume growth and higher value-added mix, and a shift to specialized ropes could limit tonnage.
Plasticated LRPC ramp depends on pending customer approvals expected within weeks; project-based orders make timing uncertain.
US tariffs and trade uncertainty; Europe and US growth targets rely on share gains against Bridon, Teufelberger and WireCo.
Thailand plant modernization execution and the INR 300 crore capex plan over 2 years.
summary.management_tone: Confident on margins, cash flow and the balance sheet, with management repeatedly citing the 20% margin benchmark and 10-12% volume target. Cautious and somewhat evasive on volume: Q4 volume growth was about 5%, and management did not quantify the order book beyond about six months of visibility.
key_quotes: The hard work of building the foundation is largely done. Now it is about execution and scaling up.
we are pretty optimistic that we should be able to improve our margins.
So, our endeavour would not be to bring it down, we would rather like to see it keep growing.
This is an important milestone for the Company.

qa_highlights.question: Why has rope volume growth remained weak despite strong margins?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said Q4 rope volume growth was about 5%, with specialised rope tonnage not linear; Middle East demand loss of about 900 tons would have taken growth to about 8%. FY27 priority is volume growth while keeping mix quality.

qa_highlights.question: Are margins sustainable given rising steel, gas and logistics costs?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said wire and LRPC increases have been passed through and rope pass-through is largely done alongside better mix; benchmark raised to a minimum of 20% operating margin from the earlier 18-19%, though quarterly mix can shift it.

qa_highlights.question: What are the capex plans and capacity additions?
qa_highlights.answer: About INR 300 crore over the next 2 years, with about 6,000 tons of rope capacity taking 70-75% of spend and the balance for specialised wires and plasticated LRPC; plasticated LRPC to step up to 8,000-9,000 tons later.

qa_highlights.question: What is the volume growth target going forward?
qa_highlights.answer: Management reiterated 10-12% volume growth across rope, specialised wires and plasticated LRPC for the next 2-3 years, and said 6-7% is the normal industry growth rate with low share in Europe and US as the upside.

qa_highlights.question: How much will plasticated LRPC ramp, and what is the timing?
qa_highlights.answer: Current volume about 2,500 tons a year; approvals expected in the next few weeks could take it to 4,000-4,500 tons, with project-based orders making timing uncertain. Black LRPC expected at about 48,000 tons, similar to last year.

qa_highlights.question: What is the company's Middle East and Thailand outlook?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said plant operations are normal and a Middle East recovery could bring reconstruction and oil and offshore opportunities; Thailand modernisation is expected to show significant improvement over about 18 months.

capex_capacity: Capex of close to INR 300 crore over the next 2 years for elevator rope capacity (about 6,000 tons of added rope capacity, 70-75% of spend), specialized wires (balance ~30%) and plasticated LRPC testing/equipment; funded from internal accruals.

Current rope capacity about 140,000 tons at ~75% utilisation; wire capacity about 80,000 tons at ~75-78% utilisation; normal LRPC capacity about 60,000 tons and plasticated LRPC about 6,000 tons, both at ~70% utilisation.

Plasticated LRPC currently about 2,500 tons a year; pending approvals expected to lift it to 4,000-4,500 tons; capacity to be stepped up to 8,000-9,000 tons in steps once current 6,000 tons is near full use.

Thailand plant (fully integrated, starts from wire rod) being modernised with added capacity for specialised cords and elevator ropes; management expects significant operating improvement over about 18 months.
Evaluating selective organic and inorganic opportunities, particularly in value-added rigging, where footprint is limited; no quantified deal pipeline given.
demand_pricing: Q4 rope volume growth about 5%; management said about 900 tons of Middle East shortfall cost roughly 3 points, implying ~8% growth otherwise.

Order book: management cited good visibility for H1 FY27 and rope demand visibility for at least 6 months; declined to quantify order book or give break-up. About 85% of business comes via replacement market.
Europe about 26% of topline with positive outlook; US rose to 9% of topline from 7%, with US market share sub-5%; Europe share about 10-12% including service centres and factory.
Realisations: international wire rope prices exceeded INR 300,000 per ton for the first time in Q4; wire and LRPC prices pass-through of steel and gas increases; LRPC revenue down 20.4% YoY in Q4.

Input costs: LPG cost up from about INR 60,000 per ton to INR 120,000-130,000 per ton; LPG use 250-300 tons a month costing about INR 2.5-3 crore a month extra; 25% of requirement to shift to natural gas via a new nearby line.
India demand growing 6-8% overall; elevator and ports segments growing faster; management expects to hold or slightly raise India share. Management said 6-7% is normal industry global growth.
Competitors named in higher-end rope segments: Bridon, Teufelberger and WireCo; Usha Martin is the only wire rope manufacturer in the GCC per management.

growth.why: Management guides 10-12% rope volume growth for the next 2-3 years (revenue midpoint ~11% used), backed by ~INR 300 crore capex over 2 years for ~6,000 t elevator rope capacity and plasticated LRPC approvals (2,500 t to 4,000-4,500 t), but order book was not quantified and rope utilisation is ~75%.
